name: Eyelash curler
summary: Opens the eyes instantly.
lead: An eyelash curler is a hand-held clamp with a curved frame and a replaceable rubber or silicone pad that bends the upper lashes into a curl. Users apply it at the lash base to make the eyes look larger and more open, often before mascara. Heated versions, introduced in the 1990s, are used to help the curl last longer.
claims: Curling lashes gives a 'prettyboy' effect and can disguise a weak eye area
Curlers can cut or damage lashes, so finger-curling with Aquaphor is a better method
A pricier, better-designed curler works better than a cheap one
Curler use can be subtle enough that new acquaintances cannot tell, and is considered attractive

name: Lash lift kit
summary: Weeks-long lash curl.
lead: A lash lift kit is a set of chemical solutions and silicone pads or rods used to give natural eyelashes a semi-permanent upward curl lasting several weeks. It is offered as a salon service and as at-home kits. The chemistry resembles a hair perm: a reducing agent loosens keratin bonds, the lashes are shaped on a rod, and a neutralizer sets them.

name: Beard growth roller
summary: If anything grows beard, it’s the minoxidil people use alongside it — not the roller.
lead: A beard growth roller is a derma roller, a hand tool with a drum of fine needles, marketed for use on the cheeks and jaw in the hope of improving patchy beard growth. It is usually discussed alongside topical minoxidil, which users apply before or after rolling. The practice is a form of microneedling adapted from scalp hair-loss routines.
claims: Dermarolling plus minoxidil gives better results than minoxidil alone.
Topical minoxidil can fill in a patchy beard.
The roller alone grows beard hair.

name: IPL hair removal device
summary: Clinical trials show real, lasting hair-count reduction. One of the most credible device categories.
lead: An IPL hair removal device is a consumer flashlamp that emits broad-spectrum pulsed light, roughly 400 to 1200 nm, to reduce unwanted body and facial hair over a series of sessions. It is a home-use version of intense pulsed light systems used in clinics. Melanin in the hair absorbs the light and converts it to heat, which damages the follicle.

name: Home laser hair removal
summary: Diode-laser cousins of IPL; similar caveats.
lead: Home laser hair removal refers to consumer devices that use a low-energy diode laser, applied by the user at home, to reduce unwanted hair growth. They work on the same general principle as professional laser systems and as home intense pulsed light (IPL) devices: pigment in the hair absorbs light, and the resulting heat is intended to damage the follicle so that regrowth slows . Typical targets are the legs, underarms, bikini line, face and torso.
claims: Alexandrite laser is the best option for fair skin with dark hair
A burning-hair smell during treatment is a good sign it is working
One session can remove most of the hair
Treatment is very painful, like being snapped with a hot rubber band

name: Electric body groomer
summary: Chest, abs, back — trimmed, not bare.
lead: An electric body groomer is a battery or mains-powered trimmer designed for hair on the chest, abdomen, back, arms and groin. It typically combines a protective guard or foil-style blade head with adjustable length settings, so that hair is cut to a chosen length rather than removed or shaved to the skin.

name: Nose + ear trimmer
summary: Nobody should ever see nose hair. $15 solves it forever.
lead: A nose and ear trimmer is a small hand-held grooming tool with a guarded rotary or oscillating blade that shortens hair at the nostril opening and the outer ear canal. Hair in the nostril is also called nasal hair or vibrissae, and its trimming is the most common way people manage visible hair there; other methods include tweezers, waxing, laser hair removal and electrolysis .

name: Epilator
summary: Pulls from the root — weeks of smooth, at the cost of some pain.
lead: An epilator is an electrical device that removes hair by mechanically grasping several hairs at once and pulling them out. The action is similar to waxing, but epilators do not use an adhesive and, unlike waxing, do not remove skin cells . They are used mostly on the legs, arms, underarms and bikini area, with smaller heads for the face.

name: Wax kit
summary: Weeks of hair-free skin.
lead: A wax kit is a set of supplies for waxing, a method of hair removal in which a sticky substance is applied to the skin, adheres to the hair, and is pulled away to remove the hair from the follicle . Home kits typically include warm (heated) wax or pre-made cold strips, applicators or spatulas, and cloth or paper strips; waxing is also offered professionally in salons .

name: Depilatory cream
summary: Dissolves surface hair painlessly. Patch-test first.
lead: A depilatory cream is a topical product that removes hair chemically. Most contain thioglycolate salts, which are commonly described as weakening the keratin of the hair shaft so that the hair can be wiped or scraped from the skin surface . It is sold for the legs, underarms, bikini area, face and torso, including men's formulations for the chest and other body hair.

name: Adjustable dumbbells
summary: Progressive overload at home. The single best evidence-to-cost ratio in this entire catalog.
lead: Adjustable dumbbells are hand-held free weights whose load can be changed, either by sliding plates onto a handle and securing them with collars, or by turning a dial or moving a pin on a selectorized set. A single adjustable pair can stand in for a whole rack of fixed dumbbells, which is why they are common in small home gyms .
claims: A home setup with adjustable dumbbells is enough to complete a full training program
Olympic dumbbell handles and plates are a better buy than adjustable dumbbells
The large plate diameter of adjustable dumbbells makes some lifts harder to hold

name: Resistance bands
summary: Real hypertrophy stimulus for the price of lunch. Also the fix for posture muscles.
lead: Resistance bands are elastic bands, loops or tubes, usually latex, rubber or fabric-covered, used for strength training and rehabilitation. Their tension rises as they are stretched, they are sold in graded and often colour-coded strengths, and they weigh little, which makes them easy to store and carry .

name: Pull-up bar
summary: Back and shoulder width — the V-taper that changes how clothes fit.
lead: A pull-up bar is a fixed horizontal bar from which the user hangs to perform pull-ups, chin-ups and hanging exercises. Bars are sold for doorway mounting, wall or ceiling mounting, and as freestanding frames. The pull-up is an upper-body strength exercise in which the body is suspended by the hands, usually gripping the bar wider than shoulder width, and pulled up so that the elbows move toward the torso .
claims: A cheap dumbbell and pull-up bar are enough for home training when a gym is unaffordable
Three sets to failure in an 8-12 rep range is the way to train each muscle with this equipment
A pull-up bar can be part of a low-cost improvised gym

name: Barbell + plates
summary: The gold standard for progressive overload.
lead: A barbell is a long steel bar with rotating sleeves at each end onto which weight plates are loaded, usually used together with a rack and a bench. The standard men's competition bar weighs 20 kg and is about 220 cm long, while the women's version weighs 15 kg and is shorter and thinner . Powerlifting bars are somewhat thicker and stiffer, and general fitness bars are often sold without competition certification .
claims: Strength training is preferable to hypertrophy training
A barbell-and-plates home gym is a low-cost option
Lifting straps raise rep counts on grip-limited barbell exercises

name: Kettlebells
summary: Strength + conditioning in one lump of iron.
lead: A kettlebell is a cast-iron or cast-steel weight shaped like a ball with a single handle, so that its centre of mass sits below and beyond the grip . That offset makes it suited to swinging and ballistic movements such as the swing, snatch, clean and jerk, which combine strength, conditioning and mobility work . Kettlebells are also the main implement in the strength sport of kettlebell lifting (girevoy sport) .

name: Dip bars
summary: Chest, shoulders, triceps with bodyweight.
lead: Dip bars, also called parallel bars or dip stations, are a pair of horizontal handles set at about hip height or higher. The user grips them with arms extended, lowers the body by bending the elbows until the shoulders are slightly below the elbows, and presses back up . They are sold as freestanding stands, wall-mounted bars, attachments for power racks and small portable units.

name: Ab wheel
summary: Brutal, effective core training. The abs still come from the kitchen.
lead: An ab wheel, also called an ab roller, is a small wheel (or pair of wheels) on an axle with a handle on each side. The user typically kneels, grips the handles, rolls the wheel forward while keeping the spine straight, and rolls back to the start . The movement is described as an anti-extension exercise, meaning the trunk muscles work to resist the lower back arching as the lever arm lengthens .

name: Weighted vest
summary: Scales bodyweight work and walks.
lead: A weighted vest is a fitted garment that adds load to the torso, usually through removable pouches or plates. Typical loads discussed for fitness use range from roughly 5 to 20 percent of body weight, and research protocols have used loads from about 5 to 40 percent of body mass in sprint studies . It can be worn for walking, hiking, bodyweight strength exercises such as push-ups, pull-ups and dips, and sports conditioning.

name: Jump rope
summary: Conditioning and calf development for pocket change.
lead: A jump rope, or skipping rope, is a cord with a handle at each end that is swung under the feet and over the head while the user jumps. It is used recreationally, in fitness programmes, in combat-sport training and in organised competition, with freestyle and speed events overseen internationally by the International Jump Rope Union .

name: Walking pad
summary: Quietly adds thousands of fat-burning steps to desk days.
lead: A walking pad is a slim, low-speed folding treadmill, usually without handrails, designed to slide under a desk, sofa or bed. Speeds on consumer models commonly top out at about 6 km/h, well below the roughly 0 to 20 km/h range described for professional fitness treadmills . It is used to add steady walking to desk-based days, often while working or watching television.

name: Smart scale
summary: Weight trends: reliable. Body-fat % reading: noisy — watch the trend, not the number.
lead: A smart scale is a bathroom scale that records body weight with load cells and sends the reading, usually by Bluetooth or Wi-Fi, to a phone app or web dashboard. Many models also report an estimated body-fat percentage and related figures, typically derived from bioelectrical impedance, in which a small electrical current is passed through the feet. In appearance-focused and physique communities the device is used mainly to log weight trends during cutting, bulking and recomposition phases.

name: Measuring tape
summary: Waist, chest, arms. The most honest progress tracker ever made.
lead: A flexible measuring tape is a ribbon of cloth, fibreglass or plastic marked with a centimetre or inch scale, used to record circumferences such as the waist, chest, upper arm and thigh. In physique and appearance tracking it complements the bathroom scale: a falling waist measurement alongside stable or rising chest and arm measurements is read by practitioners as a sign of fat loss with muscle retention or gain.

name: EMS ab belt
summary: Muscles twitch; physiques don’t change. Abs come from barbells and a deficit.
lead: An EMS ab belt is a wearable pad or belt that delivers pulses of electrical current through the skin over the abdominal wall, causing the muscles beneath to contract without voluntary effort. EMS stands for electrical muscle stimulation, also called neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES). Consumer versions are sold as a hands-free way to tone and firm the midsection, and they appear in appearance and fitness communities as a proposed shortcut to visible abdominal muscles.

name: Waist trainer
summary: Compression while worn. Zero fat loss, zero reshaping.
lead: A waist trainer is a tight, corset-style garment, usually of elastic fabric with rigid or semi-rigid boning, worn around the midsection to compress it. Modern products are marketed for daily wear over weeks or months with the aim of narrowing the waist, and they circulate widely on image-focused social media. They are descendants of the historical corset and of mid-twentieth-century waist cinchers.

name: Posture corrector brace
summary: A reminder, not a fix. The fix is training the muscles (see: resistance bands).
lead: A posture corrector brace is a strap or harness worn across the shoulders and upper back that holds the shoulders in a retracted position or prompts the wearer when they slump. Wikipedia defines posture correctors more broadly as devices intended to make the wearer aware of current posture, including braces, restrictive garments and electronic gadgets with sensors. They are sold to address rounded shoulders and slouching and appear in posture and presence discussions as a quick cosmetic aid.

name: Foam roller
summary: Short-term mobility and thoracic extension work.
lead: A foam roller is a cylinder of dense foam, commonly 30 to 90 cm long and 12 to 15 cm in diameter, on which a person rolls their body weight over muscle groups as a form of self-massage, often called self-myofascial release. It is used before or after training, and in posture-oriented routines it is also placed under the upper back for thoracic extension exercises, a drill popular among people who sit for long periods.

name: Neck training harness
summary: Actually builds neck muscle. A thicker neck changes how the whole head sits on camera.
lead: A neck training harness is a head strap or cap, connected by a chain or strap to a weight plate or resistance, that loads the neck muscles through flexion, extension and side flexion. Wrestlers, boxers and other combat-sport athletes have long used neck strengthening, and the harness has been adopted by people who want a thicker neck for appearance reasons, since neck size changes how the head and jaw sit against the shoulders in photographs and on camera.
claims: A thicker, stronger neck improves physique, posture and a 'high T' look
Neck exercises can be done without added weight if done slowly with a stretch
Training the neck three times a week for two months should show visible results

name: Chin tuck trainer
summary: Deep neck flexor work; helps the forward-head-posture profile.
lead: A chin tuck trainer is a device, commonly an inflatable pad, strap or resistance band, that provides feedback or load during chin-tuck exercises, also known as craniocervical flexion. The exercise draws the head back over the shoulders by engaging the deep neck flexors and stretching the short extensors at the base of the skull. In appearance communities it is used to address forward head posture, which they associate with a protruding chin and a weaker-looking jawline in profile photographs.
claims: The McKenzie chin tuck can cause neck hyperflexion and damage the spine, discs and occipital muscles.
Forward head posture is common among models and actors, so correcting it may be unnecessary.
Forward head posture during adolescence may contribute to maxillary forward growth.
Forward head posture causes many problems throughout the body, and correct posture becomes natural with practice.

name: Cervical pillow
summary: Neck position support at night. Hit or miss by sleeper.
lead: A cervical pillow is a contoured or roll-shaped pillow designed to support the natural curve of the neck during sleep. Designs include a raised ridge under the neck with a shallower hollow for the head, cylindrical rolls, and adjustable or semi-customized shapes, and materials range from memory foam and latex to spring and fibre fillings.

name: Standing desk / riser
summary: Posture variation beats any single "perfect" position.
lead: A standing desk is a work surface at a height suited to working on one's feet, or to sitting on a high stool. Variants include fixed-height desks, electric or crank-operated sit-stand desks that move between sitting and standing positions, and tabletop risers that sit on an existing desk and lift the keyboard and monitor.
